title: Reflections
subtitle: Things that iterate between input and output.
intro: These are just my own notes. Whether or not your own thinking lines up, you're welcome to read them as a way of looking for sparks or starting a conversation.
They keep evolving as I do.
footnote: * About the categories: «Me / Humans / Animals» is for clarity, not a claim that humans are above other animals. Where the circles overlap is where the relationships happen — Social / Care / Reciprocity; the very center, where all three meet, is Life itself.

statements.label: On how much I read
statements.text: My weakness is that I don't really read books, and I don't really learn things systematically — or more accurately, it's not that I don't want to; I just have too many things to do, so all my skills and thinking are picked up on the way to using them. On top of that, some of my thinking will naturally lack the perspective that wider reading gives, because I've read so little. I'll patiently bring more systematic reading and learning back over time. But at this stage I have this weakness — I want to say so up front.

statements.label: On similarity to others
statements.text: Anything with a reference or a source — I cite it. I have no desire to dress someone else's thinking up as my own. A few situations can happen: (1) I subconsciously read someone's work without realising it, and it became part of how I think; (2) I remembered the source once and lost it later; (3) I really did think it through on my own, and it just happens to be close to someone else's thought. If someone points me to relevant work and I do remember it being formative, I'll add the reference. If it really is my own thread, I'll bring the other person's thinking in as a conversation, as something that nudged me. Absolute truth is what I care about most. Saying nothing isn't the same as lying.

items.subtitle: Reason and desire
items.text: I have, in the name of reason, betrayed reason — when reason becomes the tool that serves desire, rather than the self-legislator, that subtle «internalised heteronomy» is exactly what moral autonomy warns against. The difference: «reason serving something» is instrumental reason; «reason answering to reason itself» is moral reason. The latter isn't opposed to the former; it's its higher-order correction, the thing that lets reason survive long-term inside a community.

items.subtitle: Care
items.text: When you're caring for someone, the core is: don't be presumptuous, don't be too soft-hearted, and don't be inexplicably hard. Understand what the life in front of you actually needs, then act on that. That, in itself, is a kind of rationality and objectivity.

items.subtitle: Self-coherence
items.text:
Not arrogant. Not avoidant. Not trampling on others, not trampling on yourself.

The core is to be self-coherent in this world — to have a place where you feel at ease, an ideal you can keep pursuing, and the means to keep yourself alive.

items.subtitle: A crack
items.text: Find a crack, and do a small thing. — Yixi

items.subtitle: Constructive thinking
items.text: If I see what looks like a circle and it turns out to be lumpy and rough, I'd be disappointed. But I know there is no real circle in this world — only irregular, rough shapes. And what I can do in a shape like that is plenty: I can hammer at it, tuck a chair into a corner, leave a skateboard by the slope. As long as a real person can use it, I'm happy and satisfied.

items.subtitle: If, suddenly
items.text: If I die unexpectedly one day, I hope what I leave behind — the thinking and the things I made — can be meaningful to some other life.

items.subtitle: Feelings and reason
items.text:
Feelings are the fuel; reason decides where the fuel flows. Calling reason cold is wrong; calling feeling foolish is another kind of intellectual arrogance.

If you have no feelings or desires and only logic, the whole structure ends up suspended in mid-air — many people end up feeling empty. But if you only have feelings without building a frame of reason, the feelings spill everywhere. The two have to feed each other.

items.subtitle: Living for myself
items.text:
It's only when you're living for yourself that you really have the courage to be disliked. Living for others' expectations leaves you forever inside anxiety and inadequacy. For me, living for myself meant finding something that mattered, to me. I don't know if I've found it — but I do know what I have to do.

From today, my meaning sits in today and tomorrow and the future — in who I want to become, in what I want to do. When obstacles come up I solve them, patiently, bit by bit. Yesterday and before don't get to decide what kind of person I am. From today, my life has a meaning that goes far beyond feelings. I won't choose self-destruction because of pain.

items.subtitle: Will vs Ability
items.text: Will and ability have to be looked at separately. You can understand a person's will — but you can't equate that with their ability. The clearest example is people who abuse their partners — they may, after each incident, slap themselves and swear it'll never happen again. Some of them really mean it. But will and ability are two different things. No matter how badly someone wants to be a certain kind of person, the part others have to take seriously is their ability. Strong will isn't proof of capacity.

items.subtitle: Desire itself
items.text: Desire often isn't satisfied by getting what it asked for — like the yam porridge in Rashomon, the obsession is the desire itself. Once you see that, you shouldn't keep being loyal to desire. Because desire sometimes leads to ruin — to trampling yourself, to trampling others.

items.subtitle: The one who reached for the stars
items.text:
There was a person
very happy with their hands — nimble, capable, able to do a lot.
But the person wanted to touch a star in the sky.

So they studied, and built longer arms.
Work didn't let up; things slowly moved forward.

Until one day, with a single «clang»,
the person's arm really did touch a star.

The person wanted to swing the arm in joy —
but the arm was too heavy to move.
The whole body had stiffened, too.

The star inched, just a little, in the sky;
the arm followed, just a little.
From the star's view, the smallest move,
and the person —
had already been pressed into a flat circle of blood.

items.subtitle: Chemical reaction
items.text:
I'm starting to understand the «not-black-and-white» part of human relationships. So often it isn't a simple a-causes-b chain — it's a chemical reaction, multiple ingredients producing a result together. If a hurt b, maybe a was already volatile, would have lit up against c, d, e or f. Or maybe what catalysed it was a-and-b together. None of that is «who's how guilty», and none of it is an excuse for the person who hurt someone. But it helps a lot — for understanding yourself, for recognising the chemistry that could turn bad, for defending against it.

It just means I try to understand causes. It doesn't erase the lines I need to draw, and it doesn't ignore decisive factors. People also have potentials of their own; ignoring those and only looking at environment misses the point of «chemistry» entirely.

items.subtitle: Group cohesion
items.text: There are so many team-bonding activities. If someone doesn't participate they get accused of being «detached, disobedient» — but the activity was never designed with people like that in mind. It's not that one activity has to fit every person (it can't), but the designers have to at least be aware of the different kinds of people who might show up, instead of imagining an ideal model. And they have to hear what's actually said, instead of assuming. Introverts, for instance, may not have the «being-with-the-crowd» need others assume they do.

items.subtitle: Carrying the problem
items.text: If you're brave enough, keep carrying the problem forward — until the cause and effect ripen and the problem falls away on its own. The way people solve problems isn't trying to find an answer. It's carrying the thing until the day you can solve it.

items.subtitle: A distorted environment
items.text:
When people were pulled from underground after the Wenchuan earthquake, they had to cover their eyes first. Their eyes had stopped adapting to sunlight.

If a person grew up in a distorted environment, the defences that grew there don't fit a healthy environment any more. That's the person who looks «out of step», the one who looks strange.

items.subtitle: Adaptation
items.text: Human instinct is to seek pleasure and avoid pain. And humans are also adaptive. Desire never gets full, and pain bends the heart.

items.subtitle: Process
items.text: The meaning of living is the process; the result is just one of the shapes the process can take. Pinning «happiness» or «being happier» onto result-milestones is hopeless — that kind of happiness gets quickly absorbed by our adaptability. I once paid off years of loans; I thought I'd feel happy and lighter for a long time, but it was a brief spell, then it became normal. Hanging the wrong kind of expectation on a result is like dangling an apple in front of a donkey — you chase the apple, get lost inside it, because the apple was never the answer.

items.subtitle: Instinct
items.text:
Human nature isn't survival. It's avoidance of pain. The reason we choose to survive is because dying-of-causes is painful. We struggle to live to avoid the suffering of hunger, sickness, extreme weather, injury.

This is also why people take their own lives. If instinct were pure survival, no one would. People choose death only when the pain of being alive exceeds the pain of dying — they choose it to stop bearing the larger pain.

Baseline good-and-bad is physical and psychological feeling. Constructed good-and-bad is meaning that we find. When the meaning grows large enough, a person stops being a creature that only chases desire.

items.subtitle: Truth
items.text:
Truth doesn't matter to most people. People prefer to believe what they want to believe — they prefer their desires get the relief of «being officially recognised as fact». A sudden disappointment or anger, most of the time, is because the events didn't match what they expected.

Learn to let go of trying to control or expect facts the way desire wants them.

items.subtitle: Not interchangeable
items.text: Human grief and human joy don't translate between people. A person's pain, without any cosmetic on it, might be ugly — real and ugly. Please understand: that's what real is.

items.subtitle: Respect
items.text: Drinkers don't get why tea-drinkers find joy in tea; tea-drinkers don't get why drinkers use alcohol to dissolve their worries. Tea and alcohol are not noble or low. You don't have to understand each other — but please respect.

items.subtitle: Fairness and ease
items.text:
«The principle of 'fairness' people derive from selfishness» — Soseki, I Am a Cat
So-called fairness is often just: I don't want to have less than someone else. If I don't have it, you shouldn't either. The day someone really has more than others, who's still chasing «fairness»?

«All worldly ease must be earned through hardship» — Soseki, I Am a Cat
True. Sugar tastes sweet only because you've drunk plain water. If you only ever drank sugar water, could you still taste the sweetness? Without a little bitterness in life — how would you taste anything good?

items.subtitle: Five Freedoms
items.text:
The fundamental principle of modern animal welfare — animals in human care should have:

· freedom from hunger and thirst
· freedom to live comfortably
· freedom from pain and injury
· freedom from fear and distress
· freedom to express their natural behaviour

items.subtitle: Racheli
items.text: Racheli says — looking at people, always so interesting. Seeing this many people, imagining all the stories behind them.

items.subtitle: Love and hate
items.text: Whether someone loves me or hates me — both are desire. Whether the love is understanding or possession, whether the hate is partial or whole-cloth — that comes down to character. An understanding love or a whole-cloth hate, I respect and thank. A possessive love or a partial hate, I filter.

items.subtitle: War
items.text:
War between countries has no good-or-evil any more — only positions. Sorrowful collective positions, where people have no choice and individuals suffer. Meaningless, but pushed forward anyway.

I won't ever go numb — many things need to be remembered. I might not say more on this here, because right now what I have is pure worry and a powerless blessing. I'll keep thinking, until there's something I can really do.

items.subtitle: Seeing the other
items.text: I won't look down on anyone. We're just walking different paths.

items.subtitle: Passion is a gift
items.text:
Talking with J, a coworker decades older. He says to the IT person — he isn't good at talking, doesn't sleep well, and «I don't have that strong love-for-something the way other people do». I said: «I think that's a kind of gift.»

Sometimes people see being quiet as a flaw, being meticulous as a virtue. But behind those — «flaw», «virtue» — there might really be the same thing: that the person loves to think. Which makes them less practised at expressing complicated content, and also makes them meticulous. The same trait makes it hard to keep a pure, hot passion going, makes it hard to fall asleep because the head won't stop. But this trait is also what gives them what they're good at, what other people don't have.

So flaw or virtue, it doesn't matter that much. What matters is knowing what your underlying trait is — how to take care of it, how to nurture it, and in that, work to become the person you want to be.

items.subtitle: «Home»
items.text: I said: «home» isn't a room — it's the whole environment of your childhood. Because I loved horror stories as a kid, reading a horror story now, when I'm scared or unsettled, calms me. So horror stories are also a kind of home to me. J says — he smells a certain crop being burned and his childhood floods back, so when he sees someone burning that crop he opens the car window to let the smell in.

items.subtitle: Maintenance
items.text:
The demo models in the CAD Room — I used to have no concept of maintaining them. I'd make them, leave them on the table, fix them when I noticed something was off. Later I realised: even the smallest models, with time, naturally bend and stick — even under normal use.

J says: small structures are like that; large machinery is like that too. And I thought — machines are like that, people are like that. Your own life is like that, the care of relationships is like that. If you don't actively maintain, they'll slowly turn — like fruit past its date.

items.subtitle: Don't presume
items.text: A classmate got bit by a mosquito; I felt worried and kept swatting it away. They refused twice and explained that it actually wouldn't itch. But for a while after the refusal I still kept swatting. I need to learn to read people's «no» — not to do something that looks helpful while ignoring the voice that's right there. Don't presume.

items.subtitle: No more hate
items.text: I don't hate anyone any more. I might endorse or not endorse a behaviour — but I won't let that escalate into a judgment on the whole person.

items.subtitle: Snake · shedding
items.text: Leaving for five days, worried about the little snake that's mid-shed and fragile. On the phone with my grandma — she said: life is very strong. Simple people, with simple sentences and a pure persistence, pass on a strength I don't have.

items.subtitle: Still gathering
items.text: Minimising pain when eating, ways to help, what I've learned keeping a snake — I'm still gathering these. More will land here in time.

items.subtitle: Still gathering
items.text: The relationship between humans and other animals — still blank for now, until I've gathered the scattered observations into something coherent.

items.subtitle: An autistic boy · trust
items.text:
I volunteered for a Diversability Week activity with kids. Brought a bag of pipe-cleaners and a little bird ocarina.

I was with one boy. He held a few red crayons and let them fall, then picked them up again. «Ding», «ding» — was he liking the feel of the crayons dropping, or the small bright sound of them landing? Other kids drew houses from their phones; people were praising them — «amazing!» I praised the boy too — «what a sound» — though I didn't say it out loud. Maybe it leaked out through my eyes, my cheeks, my fingers.

Later his mum joined another activity and I had the boy on my own. I folded pipe-cleaners into circles, flowers, fish, butterflies, and he held them with the crayons and let them fall together — the red crayons dyeing the coloured pipe-cleaners on their way down. He wasn't required to do «what the workshop expected», wasn't required to draw, wasn't required by me to play with the pipe-cleaners. He did what he wanted to do.

When we said goodbye he reached out and took my hand. That was when I noticed how trust gets built between people, and how precious that trust is. I believe understanding and company can be conveyed even without a shared language.

items.subtitle: We are not normal, just different
items.text: His mum said — she feels people abroad accept autistic kids more easily, and in China people still mostly see it as a deficit. She said: the kids are just not like us, but they're really smart. I listened carefully, and chewed on the phrase in my head again — «We are not normal, just different».

items.subtitle: A shared destiny
items.text: The community of human destiny — yes, that idea matters to me. The optimal-game-theoretic solution is ideal; that doesn't stop me adding bricks to it. The meaning of a life doesn't need to be grand — a life has meaning the moment it has subjective agency. I love every life.

items.subtitle: Definition
items.text: Life: anything with consciousness and subjective agency. I take responsibility for any life I can see.
